title: Ducky Tie
cn: 第 3 集 · 鸭子领带
novel: Ted tried to [[make amends|make amends]] with an old girlfriend he had treated badly in the past. He felt [[guilty|guilty]] about how things ended between them. He [[reached|reach]] out and asked to meet for coffee. She [[agreed|agree]] but was still [[skeptical|skeptical]] of his [[intentions|intention]]. Meanwhile, Marshall and Lily made a [[bet|bet]] with Barney. They [[challenged|challenge]] him to wear a silly ducky tie for a whole year. If Barney lost the bet, he would have to keep wearing the [[ridiculous|ridiculous]] tie everywhere he went. Barney was [[confident|confident]] he could win, but the conditions were [[tougher|tough]] than he thought. He had to [[perform|perform]] a series of difficult tasks to win the bet. The ducky tie became a running [[joke|joke]] among the group. Barney [[complained|complain]] about the tie every day, but he refused to give up. Lily and Marshall [[enjoyed|enjoy]] watching Barney suffer through the bet. Ted's meeting with his old girlfriend did not go as [[smoothly|smooth]]. She still held a [[grudge|grudge]] against him. Ted [[realized|realize]] that sometimes saying sorry is not [[enough|enough]] to fix the past. The gang laughed about their [[situations|situation]] at MacLaren's bar, and Barney [[adjusted|adjust]] to his new life with the ducky tie.

make amends.en: to do something to fix a wrong

guilty.en: feeling bad about something you did

intention.en: a plan or purpose to do something

bet.en: an agreement to risk money on something

tough.en: difficult to do or deal with

perform.en: to do a task or activity

joke.en: something said to make people laugh

complain.en: to say you are unhappy about something

grudge.en: a feeling of anger toward someone

situation.en: the state of things at a time

adjust.en: to get used to a new situation
